# maple_alert_rule (Resource)

A Maple alert rule. Signal-specific fields (`apdex_threshold_ms`, `query_builder_draft`, `raw_query_*`) are validated by the API against `signal_type`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "maple_alert_rule" "checkout_errors" {
  name            = "Checkout error rate"
  signal_type     = "error_rate"
  comparator      = "gt"
  severity        = "critical"
  threshold       = 0.05 # error rates are 0 to 1 ratios
  window_minutes  = 5
  service_names   = ["checkout"]
  tags            = ["checkout"]
  destination_ids = [maple_alert_destination.pagerduty.id]
  notes           = "Runbook: https://wiki.example.com/checkout"
}

# Warn early, page later: one rule, two tiers.
resource "maple_alert_rule" "checkout_latency" {
  name           = "Checkout p95 latency"
  signal_type    = "p95_latency"
  comparator     = "gt"
  window_minutes = 10
  service_names  = ["checkout"]
  thresholds = jsonencode([
    { severity = "warning", value = 800, destination_ids = [maple_alert_destination.team_email.id] },
    { severity = "critical", value = 2000, destination_ids = [maple_alert_destination.pagerduty.id] },
  ])
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `comparator` (String) `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `eq`, `neq`, `between` or `not_between`.
- `name` (String) Rule name, unique in the organization.
- `signal_type` (String) What the rule measures: `error_rate`, `p95_latency`, `p99_latency`, `apdex`, `throughput`, `builder_query`, `raw_query` or `uptime`.
- `window_minutes` (Number) Evaluation window, up to 1440.

### Optional

- `alert_on_no_data` (Boolean) Count a window with no data as a breach instead of skipping it.
- `apdex_threshold_ms` (Number) `apdex`: the satisfied-latency threshold T in milliseconds.
- `breaches_out_of` (Number) Fire on `consecutive_breaches_required` breaches out of this many evaluations instead of in a row (up to 30).
- `consecutive_breaches_required` (Number) Breaching evaluations in a row before the rule fires.
- `consecutive_healthy_required` (Number) Healthy evaluations in a row before an incident resolves.
- `destination_ids` (List of String) `dest_…` IDs to notify, typically `maple_alert_destination.<name>.id`.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule is evaluated. Defaults to `true`.
- `environments` (List of String) Only evaluate these `deployment.environment` values.
- `evaluation_interval_minutes` (Number) How often the rule runs: 1, 5, 10, 15, 30 or 60. Unset uses Maple's default schedule.
- `exclude_service_names` (List of String) Skip these services.
- `group_by` (List of String) Evaluate each group separately, e.g. `["service.name"]`.
- `minimum_sample_count` (Number) Skip windows with fewer samples than this.
- `notes` (String) Runbook notes included in notifications.
- `notification_template` (String) Custom notification `title` and `body`, with optional per-channel `overrides`. Write it with `jsonencode(...)`.
- `query_builder_draft` (String) `builder_query`: the query builder draft, as the dashboard's query builder saves it. Write it with `jsonencode(...)`.
- `raw_query_reducer` (String) `raw_query`: how rows reduce to one value: `identity`, `sum`, `avg`, `min` or `max`.
- `raw_query_sql` (String) `raw_query`: the SQL to evaluate.
- `renotify_interval_minutes` (Number) Re-send notifications for an open incident this often.
- `service_names` (List of String) Only evaluate these services.
- `severity` (String) `warning` or `critical`. Derived from `thresholds` when those are set.
- `tags` (Set of String) Up to 20 lowercase tags.
- `threshold` (Number) Breach threshold. Error rates are 0 to 1 ratios.
- `threshold_upper` (Number) Upper bound for `between` and `not_between`.
- `thresholds` (String) Tiered thresholds, one per severity, as an alternative to `severity` + `threshold`: a list of `{ severity, value, upper, recovery_value, destination_ids }`. Read back from the API when unset. Write it with `jsonencode(...)`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The `alrt_…` public ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import maple_alert_rule.example <id>
```
